Week1-Flowchart.title: CIA Triad: Cybersecurity Algorithm
Week1-Flowchart.algorithmIntro: A doctor needs to access a patient's medical record. The doctor first requests the required record through the hospital computer. The system checks whether the doctor is authorized to access the record. If access is not authorized, the system denies the request and stops the process. If access is authorized, the system checks whether the patient record is correct and has not been changed improperly. The system then checks whether the main record system is available. If the main system is unavailable, the system checks the backup server. The record is provided from the backup if a safe backup is available. If no safe system or backup is available, the system displays that the service is unavailable.

Week2-Flowchart.title: User Authentication: Cybersecurity Algorithm
Week2-Flowchart.algorithmIntro: A user starts the login process on a computer or laptop. The user enters a username and password. The system checks whether the login details are correct. If the details are incorrect, the login fails and the process ends. If the details are correct, the system checks whether additional authentication is required. If additional authentication is required, an OTP is sent to the user's mobile phone. The user enters the OTP and the system checks it. If the OTP is correct, the system checks the user's fingerprint or face. If the biometric information matches, access is granted. If any required verification fails, access is denied.

Week3-Flowchart.title: Phishing Email: Cybersecurity Decision Algorithm
Week3-Flowchart.algorithmIntro: A user receives an email that asks them to click a link and confirm their account details. The message looks like it came from a trusted company. The user notices that the message creates urgency and asks for sensitive information. Before clicking anything, the user should check the sender and the link. The user must decide whether the email is genuine or suspicious. If the email is suspicious, the user should not click the link and should report the message. If the email appears genuine, the user should still verify it through an official source before taking action. The safest decision is to avoid sharing sensitive information through an unexpected email.

Week4-Flowchart.title: Weak Passwords: Cybersecurity Decision Algorithm
Week4-Flowchart.algorithmIntro: A user needs to create a password for a new account. The user enters a password into the system. The system checks whether the password is strong enough. A weak password may be easy to guess or may not provide enough protection. If the password is weak, the user should create a stronger password. The user should also avoid using a password that has already been used on another account. If the password is reused, the user should choose a different password. The process continues until the password is strong and unique. The final decision is to use the strong password and complete the secure login.

Week5-Flowchart.title: Pretexting: Cybersecurity Decision Algorithm
Week5-Flowchart.algorithmIntro: A user receives a message or call from someone who claims to be an authorized person. The person asks the user to provide confidential information. The request may appear believable because the person gives a reason or creates a sense of urgency. The user should not trust the request immediately. The user's first decision should be to verify the person's identity using a trusted method. The user should then check whether the requested information is actually necessary. If the identity or request cannot be verified, the information should not be shared. If the request is legitimate, only the required information should be provided. The user should report the request if it appears suspicious.

Week6-Flowchart.title: Ransomware: Cybersecurity Response Algorithm
Week6-Flowchart.algorithmIntro: A user notices that files cannot be opened or a ransom message appears on the computer. The user should treat the situation as a possible ransomware incident. The first important decision is to stop normal activity and disconnect the affected device from the network. The user should report the incident to the security team and avoid deleting important evidence. The user should not communicate with the attacker or make a payment. The security team should check whether a safe backup is available. If a backup is available, it should be checked before it is used for recovery. If the backup is clean, the system can be restored using the verified backup. If no safe backup is available, the security team should handle the recovery process.
